opex.name: Marketing, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling cruises, advertising, and running the head office — actually down from $383M a year ago as cost discipline kicked in.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the fleet and other long-lived assets over their useful lives — a non-cash charge that grows as new ships arrive.

follow100Note: Norwegian actually got a small $7M tax benefit this quarter, which is why the tax row adds a few cents back instead of taking money out.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to the nearest $M from the release, which reports in thousands. Total cruise operating expense (crew, fuel, food, commissions and onboard costs) is treated as the cost of revenue; the tax line was a $7M benefit this quarter.
oneTimers: Restructuring costs were $2.7M in the quarter ($22.4M over the first nine months) as the turnaround program reshapes the company. Norwegian excludes them from adjusted results: adjusted net income was $514M versus $491M on a GAAP basis.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $171M — the cost of carrying $15.1B of debt — partly offset by $31M of other income, for a net $140M cost below operating profit. Interest was nearly half last year's $329M after refinancing.

segments.name: Passenger ticket
segments.note: The fares themselves, across Norwegian Cruise Line, Oceania Cruises and Regent Seven Seas. Down 5% as ticket pricing softened (Net Yield fell 6.5%), even though the fleet sailed 5% more capacity days.

segments.name: Onboard and other
segments.note: Everything guests buy around the cruise — drinks, shore excursions, spa, casino, specialty dining, plus air and hotel add-ons sold with the trip. Up 13% on stronger-than-expected close-in demand and onboard spend.

takeaways.text: Ticket revenue fell 5% to $1,946M as pricing softened, but onboard and other revenue jumped 13% to $1,001M — guests who paid less for the fare spent more once they were on the ship.
takeaways.title: Onboard spending carried the quarter

takeaways.text: Interest expense, net, dropped to $171M from $329M a year ago after refinancing. That is the main reason net income rose 17% even though operating income fell 17% to $624M — running the ships cost more, financing them cost much less.
takeaways.title: The interest bill nearly halved

takeaways.text: Occupancy hit 106.5% (some cabins held three or more guests) on 5% more capacity days. Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to about $1.70 and flagged roughly $100M of extra run-rate savings phasing in through 2028.
takeaways.title: Ships sailed more than full

verdict: Profit jumped 17% to $491M even though ticket revenue dipped — guests spent 13% more once onboard, and refinancing nearly halved the interest bill.
